preservedKevTeachingHolds.contentQualification: HOLD catalogue naming as whole 4.3 lifecycle understanding, inclusion as a compromise in this organisation or continuing activity against every asset, absence as safe/unexploited, or one universal federal/private deadline. KEV inclusion supplies reported exploitation evidence; match actual affected products/configurations and current applicable requirements. Effective main still names BOD 22-01. A CISA bulletin dated September 11 2026 instead cites BOD 26-04 and FCEB scope; its full directive was inaccessible. Thus current policy/supersession/deadlines remain unresolved, not certified by historical 22-01 references. Current stem removes agency-deadline wording but the main requires this precise teaching hold. Source hard to easy uncalibrated. No live catalogue count, entry, affected host, legal advice or deadline is verified.

HOLD a universal 15-day KEV rule, every Critical finding as one fixed SLA, a released patch as deployed/validated remediation, or interim controls as eliminating every exploit path. Applicable deadlines, emergency authority, business continuity, rollback and actual mitigation coverage remain requirements; validation/compromise investigation can be needed. This is one composite response choice, not independently scored assessment/mitigation/patching skills. Current scenario removes authored blanket framework 15-to-30-day and 24-to-72-hour claims. Historic BOD 22-01 statements are not a verified current deadline: a September 2026 CISA bulletin refers to BOD 26-04, whose full requirements were not retrievable here. Preserve the unresolved current-policy hold rather than inferring supersession details. No service, policy, patch, attack or interim control is changed.
